clue.text: Remove work of art

definitions.meaning: to take it away or extract it

explanation.surface: An instruction to take a painting off the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to withdraw or extract; as a noun it is a piece of non-figurative art.

clue.text: Claiming everyone, say, has imbibed drink

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: one piece that has imbibed another takes it inside

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as say does
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: Asserting that the whole group has been drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Asserting something without proof, as in an accusation.

clue.text: Do German, having first succeeded with Asian language

parts.note: s is an abbreviation for succeeded in family trees
Hindi is a language of India

explanation.surface: A German speaker who learnt an Indian language early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having first' puts S at the very start, before HINDI and G.
explanation.definitionFit: A do is a party, and a lively party is a shindig.

clue.text: Artist given stick in foreign capital

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, stands for an artist
a bat is a stick used in sport

explanation.surface: A painter is handed a club while abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Morocco.

clue.text: Prepares to fire weapon, catching head of poor bird

indicators.note: the pair catch a letter between them, holding it inside

parts.note: cocks a gun readies it for firing
an arrow is a weapon

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A hunter gets ready to shoot at a scrawny bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' puts P (head of 'poor') between COCKS and ARROW.
explanation.definitionFit: A cock sparrow is a male house sparrow.

clue.text: Electrician leaves vehicle by front of shop

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter, here taken from shop

parts.note: a driver who leaves a car somewhere parks it

explanation.surface: A tradesman abandons the van outside a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sparks' is British slang for an electrician; S (front of 'shop') comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparks is the informal British nickname given to an electrician, from the sparks of the trade.

clue.text: A group of sailors in predicament on American mountain

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it
one piece in another sits inside it

parts.note: a pass is a difficult situation, as in 'come to a pretty pass'
RN is the Royal Navy
US means American

explanation.surface: Navy men stuck on a mountain in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: ARN goes inside PASS, then US is added below.
explanation.definitionFit: Parnassus is the Greek mountain sacred to Apollo and the Muses.

clue.text: See thug collar Scottish chap

parts.note: a ruff is a frilled collar
Ian is a common Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: Watch a hooligan grab a Scotsman by the collar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collar' looks like a verb, to seize, but it is the noun RUFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A brutal, violent person.

clue.text: Case girl encountered at hospital

parts.note: she refers to a girl

explanation.surface: A legal case involving a woman met at a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a close-fitting cover for a blade.

clue.text: Easy-going learner gets two kinds of help

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate
aid is one kind of help
to back someone is to help them, support being the second kind

explanation.surface: A student is given plenty of assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: The one phrase 'two kinds of help' supplies both AID and BACK.
explanation.definitionFit: A relaxed, unhurried person is described with this informal adjective.

clue.text: Dessert? Just a small amount

definitions.meaning: a pudding of sponge, fruit, custard and cream
a tiny quantity, as in 'a little bit'

explanation.surface: Asking whether only a little pudding is on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: The British layered pudding shares its name with a word for an insignificant quantity.

clue.text: Togged out, after discarding one good piece of material

indicators.note: out here means rearranged, so the remaining letters are put into a new order
discarding means a letter is thrown away from the word before the anagram

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good, and one tells us to drop only a single G

explanation.surface: Someone all dressed up throws away a fine piece of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after discarding' removes one G from TOGGED to leave TOGED, and 'out' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: A godet is a triangular insert of fabric sewn into a skirt to give flare.

clue.text: Left-winger, thus, is heading CIA record of names

indicators.note: one piece heading another stands in front of it, so these letters lead

parts.note: so means in this way, thus
taken as written
a list records names

explanation.surface: A radical sees the American intelligence agency keeping a register.
explanation.definitionFit: A person on the political left supports socialism.

clue.text: Talk about line out of place in item of correspondence

indicators.note: talk is placed about the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: chatter is idle talk

indicators.note: out of place says the letters of line are not in their right order

explanation.surface: Discussion of a misplaced line in a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of place' rearranges LINE to INLE, which 'about' puts inside CHATTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter that asks each recipient to send copies on to others.

clue.text: No lasagne will have turned out wrong .. thanks to her?

indicators.note: letters that have turned out wrong are jumbled into a different order

explanation.surface: Praise for a cookery writer whose recipes guarantee success with pasta bakes.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal 'have turned out wrong' works on NO LASAGNE WILL; Nigella Lawson is a British TV cook and food writer.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous television cook is the person credited for a dish that never fails.

clue.text: Diva's debut in surprisingly classier recording

indicators.note: one piece in another sits inside it
surprisingly hints the letters come out in an unexpected order
a debut is a first appearance, so the opening letter

explanation.surface: A singer's first album is unexpectedly upmarket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges CLASSIER into LASERISC, and D (debut of 'Diva's') goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: An optical disc used to store video before the DVD.

clue.text: Was concerned about large amount put in a box

indicators.note: the first piece goes about the other, enclosing it

parts.note: cared means was concerned
a ton, or tons, is a large amount

explanation.surface: Someone worried about a heap of things to pack.
explanation.definitionFit: Packed in a cardboard container.

clue.text: For some Italians, Venice unfortunately is in a real mess

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone awry, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Venetians lament the poor state of their lagoon city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Most Serene, an old title of the Venetian Republic, is still a nickname for the city among Italians.

clue.text: Composer, meek sort, meeting queen with a little trepidation

parts.note: a lamb is a gentle, meek person
ER is Elizabeth Regina

indicators.note: a little of a word here is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: A timid musician meets the monarch nervously.
explanation.walkthrough: Constant Lambert was a British composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Constant Lambert wrote The Rio Grande.

clue.text: Travelling back during spring?

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in winter'
a bound is a spring or leap

explanation.surface: A journey home in the springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' suggests the season but is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading homewards or towards a place, as an incoming train does.

clue.text: Put question to a state policeman in Africa

parts.note: to ask is to put a question
RI is Rhode Island, a US state

explanation.surface: Questioning an African officer about the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A local soldier or police officer in East Africa under colonial rule.

clue.text: Type of belt British have included in uniform

indicators.note: one piece is included within another, so it sits inside it

parts.note: uniform means consistent, the same throughout
to own is to have

explanation.surface: A military belt is part of a British soldier's kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' is an adjective here, not the soldier's outfit; BROWN goes inside SAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sam Browne is an officer's leather belt with a strap over the shoulder.

clue.text: What one might wear for riding practice

definitions.text: What one might wear for riding
definitions.meaning: a riding outfit, the jacket and skirt worn on horseback

explanation.surface: A question of the right outfit for horse riding.
explanation.definitionFit: A riding outfit is called by this name, which also means a settled custom.

clue.text: Bird hidden by another one

indicators.note: hidden by tells us the word lies concealed in the next words

explanation.surface: One bird concealed by another.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-legged wading bird.

clue.text: Man or woman giving a list of words

parts.note: lexis is the vocabulary of a language, its stock of words

explanation.surface: Someone provides a vocabulary list.
explanation.definitionFit: A first name used for both sexes.

clue.text: Top performer beginning to take pot

parts.note: a start is a beginning
an urn is a pot or vessel

explanation.surface: A leading entertainer starts by taking a turn at the jackpot.
explanation.definitionFit: The headline act on a variety bill is its chief attraction.

clue.text: International law not broken

parts.note: an act of parliament is a law

explanation.surface: Global legislation that has never been breached.
explanation.definitionFit: Whole and undamaged.

clue.text: Recurrent noise suppressed by secret society in island

indicators.note: something suppressed by another is held down inside it

parts.note: a triad is a Chinese secret criminal society

indicators.note: recurrent read as running back, so the word for noise is turned round

parts.note: din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A gang on an island silences a repeated racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recurrent' turns DIN into NID, which goes inside TRIAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The larger of the two islands of a Caribbean nation.
